summary: The note discusses the St. Louis Cardinals' long history of seasons, focusing on their extended period of failure after joining the National League in 1892. It notes they had only five winning seasons in 30 years and finished last seven times until 1921. It also points out that they have avoided finishing last in the NL since 1918, and that they missed the World Series in the 1950s, 1970s, and 1990s while remaining competitive in those decades.
one_line: Overview of the St. Louis Cardinals' seasons, covering their losing early NL years and their later avoidance of last-place finishes.
key_facts: The St. Louis Cardinals joined the National League in 1892.
The Cardinals played only five winning seasons in their first 30 years in the National League.
The Cardinals finished last seven times from their entrance to the NL until 1921.
The Cardinals have not finished in last place in the National League since 1918.
The Cardinals' streak of avoiding last place in the NL since 1918 is by far the longest in the NL.
The Cardinals failed to reach the World Series in the 1950s, 1970s, and 1990s.
The Cardinals were regularly a competitive team in the 1950s, 1970s, and 1990s despite not reaching the World Series.
The note describes the period beginning in 1892 as the only extended period of failure the Cardinals have experienced.
